acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Arachnids family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Stalker, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Tripline Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Barbed legs, venom-slick fangs, bright abdomen patterning, first web decorations, and still no humanoid torso.
Signature mechanic: Barbed Line: the pure-spider Stalker hooks silk between two barbed forelegs, sweeps the tripline forward, and bites only targets it catches.
battlefieldDuty: Repeat ambush pressure by stretching one visible tripline between barbed legs and following with venomous fangs.
constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity silk, venom, amber, eye glow, wet fang sheen, web vibration, and spinneret thread remain biological or crafted spider motifs rather than Water, Fire, Wind, or magical affinity evidence.

Motion stays anatomical and tensile: eight legs load visible joints, ordinary silk stretches and breaks, spinnerets track thread origins, venom clings to fangs, and eye light remains bounded to existing eyes without environmental wake.
counterplay: Cut the visible line at either leg or step behind the abdomen while both forelegs remain spread. Affinity signal: The loaded leg joint, aligned eye gap, exposed spinneret, silk knot, or throne anchor preserves each form's established weak point.
forbiddenTreatments: Treating ordinary silk, venom sheen, eye glow, wet fangs, or vibrating webs as affinity construction
identityInvariants: A bulbous abdomen, eight jointed legs arching around the body, clustered eyes, fangs, and spinnerets remain legible; a humanoid torso is added only from T3 onward.
Black, charcoal, deep violet, blood-red markings, pale silk white, and green, red, or amber eye accents form the source palette.
Chitin, coarse bristle, silk, bone, amber, venom sheen, and eye settings remain physically distinct family materials.
Web decorations, silk robes, egg sacs, wrapped prey, jeweled eye settings, and layered drapery communicate escalation.
Leg load, spinneret direction, fang posture, silk tension, and eye cluster alignment preserve readable attack and recovery states.
telegraph: Bright abdomen patterning flattens, venom-slick fangs lift, and ordinary silk tightens between two barbed legs.
